title: Rate of temperature rise of a liquid heated by a radioactive nuclide produced at a constant rate
summary: A reactor makes nuclide X at a constant rate alpha; its decays heat a liquid. The nuclei build up to alpha/lambda, so the heating starts at zero and levels off: dT/dt = (alpha E0/ms)(1 - e^-lambda t) - option A, found by fitting the options to the thermometer's measured rate.
subject: Physics
topic: Radioactive nuclide produced at a constant rate - build-up to saturation and the heat its decays deliver
subtopics: Radioactive decay law: activity = lambda N
Production at a constant rate with decay: dN/dt = alpha - lambda N
Energy released per decay heating a liquid: ms dT/dt = E0 lambda N
concepts: dN/dt = alpha - lambda N with N(0) = 0 gives N = (alpha/lambda)(1 - e^-lambda t)
The activity lambda N = alpha(1 - e^-lambda t) starts at zero and rises to alpha, when decay balances production
With no heat loss ms dT/dt = E0 lambda N, so dT/dt = (alpha E0/ms)(1 - e^-lambda t) - option A
Check every candidate at t = 0 (nothing has decayed, so no heating) and as t -> infinity (activity = alpha): only A passes both
Traps: (B) grows without limit; (C) puts lambda where the production rate belongs; (D) heats at full power before any nucleus exists
After the reactor stops, the nuclei present keep decaying: decay heat falls as e^-lambda t

methods: MathonGo solution (their Q20 = Physics Q.2) read first as the conceptual reference; its answer (A) agrees
Independent solve: dN/dt = alpha - lambda N -> N = (alpha/lambda)(1 - e^-lambda t); ms dT/dt = E0 lambda N -> (A)
Symbolic (sympy): the rate equation solved with N(0) = 0; E0 lambda N/(ms) equals option A exactly; B, C, D differ
Convolution: the activity built from every nucleus's survival probability e^-lambda(t - tau) equals alpha(1 - e^-lambda t) within 1e-6
Monte Carlo of individual nuclei made at random and decaying at random (200 runs): the activity follows alpha(1 - e^-lambda t) within 3 %
Energy bookkeeping: the temperature rise from (A) equals E0 x (made - still present)/(ms) at every t
Options audited: at t = 0 (D) is E0(alpha - lambda)/ms, not 0; as t -> infinity (B) diverges and (C) tends to lambda E0/ms
